properties.project_name: Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Hall
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-18 for Mission Bay's UCSF campus pass: real OSM building footprint. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the notes were corrected in place: the Japanese seismic technology was buckling-restrained braces (Forell: 'we worked directly with Nippon Steel in Japan to design and procure Buckling-Restrained Braces ... brand new to California seismic engineering practice'), not base isolation; '171,600 sq ft' appears in no source read (Forell gives 165,000; the May 2000 Regents item gives 170,965 gsf). The April 2005 design-award mention rests on a UCSF news page that returns 403 to automated fetches (only its URL slug was seen).
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint, not a hand trace or plan estimate. This is the opposite situation from Mission Bay's condo-mapped residential towers (Avalon, Radiance, etc.): here, ONE large Assessor land parcel spans SEVERAL UCSF buildings (confirmed against data/raw/parcels.geojson and DataSF's Assessor tax roll -- e.g. blklot 8711507 at 675 Nelson Rising Lane alone is ~13 acres, far larger than any single building on it), so using the parcel boundary per building would make multiple records overlap and double-count the same ground. The real building footprint is the only non-overlapping, honest shape for each one.
properties.notes: ~165,000 sq ft (Forell), five stories; the May 2000 Regents design-approval item for the building believed to be this one gives 170,965 gsf. Architect Pelli Clarke Pelli with Flad Architects; notable for early use in California of buckling-restrained braces designed and procured with Nippon Steel in Japan (Forell), not seismic base isolation. Opening year is genuinely contested across sources (2002 vs. 2004 vs. one secondary '2005' reference); 2004 is the best-supported reading (UCSF's own historical archive, and a Rock Hall design-award mention in April 2005 implying it was already open), but flagged here as approximate pending a firmer primary source.
